children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

You live in the UK.

  - Alex is 8 years old and does not live with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Someone who lives with the child is already claiming
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know about the children you're claiming for.

**First, could you tell me:**

1. **How many children** are you looking to claim Child Benefit for?
2. **For each child, what is their age** (or date of birth)?

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thanks for that information. So you're looking to claim Child Benefit for **Alex, who is 8 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, that's a good starting point. Let me navigate through the eligibility checks.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check a few more details about Alex.

**Question 1: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

(For an 8-year-old, the answer is typically "yes" - most children this age aren't working. I'm just confirming this.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, he's not working at all. He's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's what I expected for an 8-year-old. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 2: Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

(For an 8-year-old in primary school, this should typically be "yes" - they wouldn't normally receive these benefits.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 3: Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

(Again, at 8 years old in primary school, he almost certainly wouldn't be - just confirming.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. He's only 8, he's just at primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! As expected. Let me move forward to the next important check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Question 4: Do you normally live in the UK?**

To help clarify, I'm asking about whether you (the person claiming Child Benefit) normally reside in the UK. There are also some special circumstances that might apply if you have a specific residency status. Does any of the following apply to you:

- You normally live in the UK, or
- You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or
- You have pre-settled status and are working, actively seeking work, studying, have sufficient resources, or are a family member of an EEA/Swiss national, or
- You're a Crown servant living abroad in certain qualifying countries?

What's your residency situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm in Leeds.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's straightforward - you normally live in the UK, so you meet the residency requirements. Let me move on to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 5: Are you responsible for Alex?**

This means either:
- You live with Alex, or
- You contribute to his upkeep (for example, paying for food, clothes, pocket money, housing, or presents), or
- You're paying maintenance under a court order or agreement

Which of these applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me - he lives with his mum, my ex-partner.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. So Alex lives with his mum, not with you. However, you may still be able to claim if you contribute to his upkeep.

**Can you tell me: Do you contribute to Alex's upkeep?** 

This could include things like:
- Paying towards his food, clothes, or pocket money
- Contributing to his housing costs
- Buying him presents or other necessities
- Making regular payments (weekly, monthly, or lump sums)

Or do you have a court order or agreement for maintenance payments towards Alex's care?

If you don't contribute financially to Alex's upkeep, then unfortunately you wouldn't meet the responsibility requirement for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not currently contributing financially to his care.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Unfortunately, based on the eligibility rules, if you don't live with Alex and you're not contributing financially to his upkeep, then you don't meet the responsibility requirement for Child Benefit.

Let me confirm this outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me provide you with the formal outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Assessment Result: **INELIGIBLE** ❌

**Why you're not eligible:**

To claim Child Benefit, you must be **responsible for the child**, which means either:
1. **Living with the child**, or
2. **Contributing to their upkeep** (food, clothes, housing, pocket money, presents, etc.), or
3. **Paying maintenance under a court order or agreement**

In your case:
- Alex lives with his mother (not with you)
- You're not currently making financial contributions towards his care

Therefore, you don't meet the responsibility requirement.

**What you could do:**

If your circumstances change in the future and you:
- Start contributing financially to Alex's upkeep, or
- Alex comes to live with you, or
- You have a formal maintenance agreement in place

Then you may become eligible to claim. You can re-apply at that point.

Alternatively, his mother (who he lives with) may be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him, provided she meets the other eligibility criteria.

If you have any questions or if your situation changes, feel free to reach out for another assessment.

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old and meets the age requirement (under 16). He is not working full-time, not receiving benefits in his own name, and is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship. You also meet the residency requirement as you normally live in the UK. However, you do not meet the responsibility requirement for Child Benefit. To be eligible, you must either live with Alex or contribute financially to his upkeep (at least an amount equivalent to Child Benefit). Since you don't live with Alex and you're not currently contributing financially to his care, you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex because you do not meet the responsibility requirement. While Alex meets all the child eligibility criteria (age under 16, not working full-time, not receiving disqualifying benefits, and you meet UK residency requirements), the rules require that the claimant must either live with the child or contribute to their upkeep. Since Alex lives with his mother and you are not currently making financial contributions towards his care, you cannot claim Child Benefit for him.">
